description: Fix the Cognito redirect_mismatch that fails the realtime-battle HOST login while keeping the admin-page login working. The fix spans BOTH the frontend OAuth helper and the CDK Cognito app-client config, which must be made mutually consistent (byte-for-byte matching redirect_uri / callback+logout URLs). Chosen scheme (option a): canonicalize the public-app host redirect to the ROOT ('origin + /'), which is how Amplify actually serves the site, and register that exact string in Cognito. The admin page keeps using 'origin + /admin.html'. This is a single coherent unit of work because a change to only one side would leave the mismatch (or introduce a new one). NOTE: no build/test can run in this INTEGRATIONS_ONLY sandbox (npm registry 403); implement correct-by-construction and verify by reading + updating the jest assertions.
steps: frontend/src/auth.ts: Change loginUrl() and logoutUrl() to accept an EXPLICIT redirect target, instead of deriving it from adminPageUrl(). Suggested signature: `loginUrl(redirectUri: string)` and `logoutUrl(redirectUri: string)` (encodeURIComponent it into redirect_uri= / logout_uri= respectively). Keep everything else identical (response_type=token, scope=openid+email+profile, client_id).

frontend/src/auth.ts: Add two small helpers that produce the canonical, Cognito-registered targets so call sites never derive from pathname: `adminRedirectUri()` returning `window.location.origin + '/admin.html'` and `publicRedirectUri()` returning `window.location.origin + '/'` (canonical ROOT). Add a prominent comment stating these strings MUST match the callbackUrls/logoutUrls registered in lib/quiz-app-stack.ts byte-for-byte (scheme, host, path, trailing slash), and that Amplify serves the public app at the ROOT so the browser is at 'origin + /' after redirect (not '/index.html').

frontend/src/auth.ts: Keep adminPageUrl() (origin + pathname) ONLY for captureTokenFromHash()'s history.replaceState target so the fragment is stripped in place on whatever page the browser actually landed on. Add a comment clarifying adminPageUrl() is intentionally NOT used for the OAuth redirect_uri anymore (that must be the canonical registered string), only for cleaning the current URL after token capture.

frontend/src/pages/AdminPage.tsx: Update the loginUrl()/logoutUrl() call sites (handleLogin ~line 136, handleLogout ~line 143) to pass adminRedirectUri() so the admin page keeps using origin + '/admin.html' (unchanged behavior, but now explicit).

frontend/src/pages/BattlePage.tsx: Update the loginUrl()/logoutUrl() call sites (~lines 408 and 414) to pass publicRedirectUri() so the battle host redirect_uri is the canonical ROOT origin + '/', which matches how Amplify serves the public app and the new Cognito registration.

lib/quiz-app-stack.ts: Update callbackUrls and logoutUrls (currently `${adminAppBaseUrl.valueAsString}/admin.html` and `${adminAppBaseUrl.valueAsString}/index.html`). Keep the `/admin.html` entry unchanged. Replace the `/index.html` entry with `${adminAppBaseUrl.valueAsString}/` (canonical ROOT) so it matches the browser's redirect_uri for the battle host. Add a comment explaining the ROOT canonicalization: Amplify serves the public app at the root URL, so the host's redirect_uri is 'origin + /' (with trailing slash, no index.html), and this string MUST match frontend/src/auth.ts publicRedirectUri() byte-for-byte.

lib/quiz-app-stack.ts: Update the includeLocalhostCallback block accordingly: keep pushing 'http://localhost:8080/admin.html', and replace 'http://localhost:8080/index.html' with 'http://localhost:8080/' (trailing slash) for both callbackUrls and logoutUrls, so local dev of the public app at the root is also trusted. Keep the existing gating logic unchanged.

lib/quiz-app-stack.ts: Update the explanatory comment block above callbackUrls (the one describing the '/index.html' host view) so it now describes the ROOT canonicalization rather than '/index.html'.

test/quiz-app-stack.test.ts: The current test file does NOT assert callback/logout URLs. Add a focused test that synthesizes the stack (default adminAppBaseUrl parameter is http://localhost:8080) and asserts the AWS::Cognito::UserPoolClient CallbackURLs / LogoutURLs contain the expected values for the chosen scheme. With the default param and includeLocalhostCallback defaulting to true, the URLs are Fn::Join/Fn::Sub tokens over the CfnParameter for the production entries; assert the DECIDABLE localhost entries 'http://localhost:8080/admin.html' and 'http://localhost:8080/' are present and that 'http://localhost:8080/index.html' is NOT present. Use Match.arrayWith for CallbackURLs/LogoutURLs. This test must be written so it would FAIL if the '/index.html'->'/' change were reverted.

README.md: Update the authentication-model section (the paragraph mentioning adding '/index.html' to the callback/logout URLs, around lines 255-258) and the deploy step 4 (around lines 380-392) to describe the ROOT canonicalization. Explicitly document that the fix requires BOTH: (1) redeploy the backend so Cognito's callback/logout URLs are updated, passing adminAppBaseUrl EXPLICITLY (it reverts to the localhost default otherwise, which is part of why login failed): `npx cdk deploy --parameters adminAppBaseUrl=https://main.d2uwsqpk41y7so.amplifyapp.com -c includeLocalhostCallback=false`; AND (2) rebuild/redeploy the frontend: `cd frontend && npm install && npm run build`, then redeploy via Amplify. State that adminAppBaseUrl must be the real Amplify domain and that the host now returns to the site ROOT (origin + '/'), not '/index.html'.
acceptance_criteria: The battle host's redirect_uri (from BattlePage.tsx via publicRedirectUri()) is exactly window.location.origin + '/' and matches a Cognito-registered callback AND logout URL (`${adminAppBaseUrl}/` in lib/quiz-app-stack.ts).

The admin page's redirect_uri (from AdminPage.tsx via adminRedirectUri()) is exactly window.location.origin + '/admin.html' and still matches the registered `${adminAppBaseUrl}/admin.html` callback and logout URL (admin login remains working).

lib/quiz-app-stack.ts callbackUrls and logoutUrls each contain `${adminAppBaseUrl.valueAsString}/admin.html` and `${adminAppBaseUrl.valueAsString}/`; the '/index.html' entries are removed; localhost variants (when includeLocalhostCallback) are 'http://localhost:8080/admin.html' and 'http://localhost:8080/'.

frontend/src/auth.ts loginUrl()/logoutUrl() take an explicit redirect target; the redirect_uri is no longer derived from window.location.pathname; captureTokenFromHash still strips the fragment on the current page via adminPageUrl().
Frontend dependencies remain exactly react + react-dom with no lockfile changes; JWT authorizer, WebSocket API, and scoring are untouched.
test/quiz-app-stack.test.ts asserts the new callback/logout URL scheme and would fail if the change were reverted; the pre-existing tests remain semantically valid.
verification: Read frontend/src/auth.ts, AdminPage.tsx, BattlePage.tsx and lib/quiz-app-stack.ts side by side and confirm the exact strings match byte-for-byte: admin => origin + '/admin.html' vs `${adminAppBaseUrl}/admin.html`; host => origin + '/' vs `${adminAppBaseUrl}/`.
Confirm no '/index.html' remains in the OAuth redirect path or Cognito callback/logout URLs (grep lib/quiz-app-stack.ts and frontend/src/auth.ts).

Attempt `npm test` and `npx cdk synth` at repo root; if the sandbox blocks them (INTEGRATIONS_ONLY npm 403), record that and rely on reading. Document `npm test` + `npx cdk synth` as the user's real verification commands.
Confirm README documents both the backend redeploy (with explicit adminAppBaseUrl) and the frontend rebuild/redeploy.
findings:
Implemented option (a) ROOT canonicalization across both sides. frontend/src/auth.ts: loginUrl(redirectUri)/logoutUrl(redirectUri) now take an explicit redirect target; added adminRedirectUri()=origin+'/admin.html' and publicRedirectUri()=origin+'/'; adminPageUrl() kept ONLY for captureTokenFromHash()'s history.replaceState. AdminPage.tsx passes adminRedirectUri(); BattlePage.tsx passes publicRedirectUri(). lib/quiz-app-stack.ts: callbackUrls/logoutUrls now hold `${adminAppBaseUrl}/admin.html` and `${adminAppBaseUrl}/`; localhost variants are 'http://localhost:8080/admin.html' and 'http://localhost:8080/'; the '/index.html' entries were removed; comment block rewritten to describe ROOT canonicalization and byte-for-byte matching with auth.ts. test/quiz-app-stack.test.ts: added a focused test asserting CallbackURLs/LogoutURLs contain the localhost admin.html and '/' entries and NOT '/index.html' (fails if reverted). README.md: auth-model paragraph and deploy step 4 updated to document ROOT canonicalization and that BOTH a backend redeploy (explicit adminAppBaseUrl + includeLocalhostCallback=false) AND a frontend rebuild/redeploy are required. Verified redirect strings match byte-for-byte: admin origin+'/admin.html' vs `${adminAppBaseUrl}/admin.html`; host origin+'/' vs `${adminAppBaseUrl}/`. No '/index.html' remains in any OAuth redirect path or Cognito URL array (remaining '/index.html' mentions in the stack are old-CloudFront-rewrite comments and the fix explanation). Frontend deps unchanged (react + react-dom, no lockfile). JWT authorizer, WebSocket API, and scoring untouched. VERIFICATION NOT RUN in sandbox: INTEGRATIONS_ONLY blocks npm (no node_modules present; `npm test` failed on a missing proxy-bootstrap preload and cannot install from the 403 registry). Correct-by-construction + reading used instead. User's real verification commands: `npm test` (jest) and `npx cdk synth` at repo root, plus `cd frontend && npm install && npm run build`.

REVIEW FOLLOW-UP (2026-09-05-224913-review.md, verdict APPROVED, 2 non-blocking findings):
Issue 1 (trailing-slash footgun on adminAppBaseUrl): FIXED at the source rather than with a no-op token .replace(). Because adminAppBaseUrl is a CfnParameter, `.valueAsString` is a synth-time token and a JS `.replace(/\/$/, '')` on it silently does nothing (the review explicitly warned against shipping that). Instead I added an `allowedPattern` `^(https?://)[^\s]*[^/\s]$` (plus a `constraintDescription`) to the CfnParameter, so CloudFormation VALIDATES the value at deploy time and REJECTS any trailing slash (and any value missing an http(s) scheme) before the stack proceeds. This is token-safe and actively prevents the doubled-slash `//` that would reintroduce redirect_mismatch, which is stronger than documentation alone. Verified the regex against JS RegExp: accepts `http://localhost:8080` and `https://main.d2uwsqpk41y7so.amplifyapp.com`; rejects the same with a trailing `/` and a scheme-less host (the default param value passes its own pattern). Also strengthened the CfnParameter `description`, added a code comment at the URL-construction site explaining why raw concatenation is now safe (the pattern guarantees no trailing slash) and why a `.replace()` would be a no-op, and added a prominent README note next to the deploy command documenting the no-trailing-slash requirement. Added a focused jest test ('adminAppBaseUrl parameter rejects a trailing slash at deploy time') that reads the synthesized parameter's AllowedPattern and asserts it accepts trailing-slash-free origins and rejects trailing slashes / missing schemes; it would FAIL if the AllowedPattern were removed or weakened.
Issue 2 (host token captured only after entering the host view): ACKNOWLEDGED and intentionally LEFT AS-IS. The review explicitly marks it pre-existing and OUT OF SCOPE for this redirect-matching fix; captureTokenFromHash() still runs inside the host view and strips the fragment via adminPageUrl(). No behavior change made here per the review guidance.
VERIFICATION for the follow-up: still INTEGRATIONS_ONLY (no node_modules, npm 403), so jest/cdk synth cannot run; the allowedPattern regex was verified with a standalone node RegExp check (all 5 cases pass). Correct-by-construction otherwise.
